intent.purpose: Track harness deficiencies and drive corrective actions — spec deviations, ambiguities, and operational incidents with root cause analysis, remediation, and prevention layer assignment

incidents.title: Hook scripts deployed without backup or interactive review
incidents.observation: setup-user-hooks.sh/.ps1 use direct cp/Copy-Item for hook scripts. No backup_file call before overwrite, no deploy_managed_file interactive review, no adopt/skip/merge options.
incidents.expected: .claude/rules/managed-file-deployment.md requires backup before write and interactive diff review for shell script deployment type. .claude/rules/config-file-safety.md requires backup before overwrite.
incidents.impact: User customizations to hook scripts in ~/.claude/hooks/ are silently overwritten on every aitools install. No way to review changes or adopt local modifications back to source.
incidents.discoveryContext: Filed during governance plan design session. Audited: managed-file-deployment.md, config-file-safety.md, setup-user-hooks.sh. Session: 2026-03-13.
incidents.suggestedResolution: Upgrade to deploy_managed_file (same as markdown type). Adopt target: shared/hooks/<filename> in aitools repo.

incidents.title: Bash scripts missing backup_file before JSON config merge
incidents.observation: setup-user-hooks.sh and setup-user-mcp.sh do NOT call backup_file before settings.json merge. Their PowerShell counterparts DO call Backup-File.
incidents.expected: .claude/rules/config-file-safety.md 'Backup before overwrite': caller MUST call backup_file / Backup-File before the merge write for JSON config type.
incidents.impact: If a bash merge corrupts settings.json, there is no backup to restore from. PowerShell has the backup. Platform parity violation — same operation has different safety guarantees per platform.
incidents.discoveryContext: Filed during governance plan design session. Audited: config-file-safety.md, setup-user-hooks.sh, setup-user-mcp.sh, their .ps1 counterparts. Session: 2026-03-13.
incidents.suggestedResolution: Add backup_file call in bash scripts before Node.js merge, matching the PowerShell pattern.

incidents.title: JSON config merges have no interactive review
incidents.observation: All JSON config merges proceed silently. Clobber detection blocks on field loss, but there is no 'here is what will change, proceed?' prompt showing managed field diffs.
incidents.expected: .claude/rules/interactive-menus.md defines JSON field-level review with current → proposed display. No setup script implements this pattern for JSON configs.
incidents.impact: Users cannot review what changed in settings.json, cli-config.json, or mcp.json before the write. Silent merges erode trust — users don't know what aitools changed on their machine.
incidents.discoveryContext: Filed during governance plan design session. Audited: interactive-menus.md, setup-user-hooks.sh, setup-user-mcp.sh, setup-user-cursor.sh. Session: 2026-03-13.
incidents.suggestedResolution: Add field-level review menu showing changed managed fields with old → new values. Pattern defined in interactive-menus.md 'JSON field-level review'.

incidents.title: Cursor MCP disable is project-scoped, not user-scoped
incidents.observation: agent mcp disable stores disable state per-project, not per-user. Setup script runs from the aitools repo directory only. Other projects see vercel/webflow as enabled.
incidents.expected: .claude/rules/tool-lifecycle.md 'MCP server disable scope' documents this asymmetry. No setup script accounts for it.
incidents.impact: Projects other than aitools see vercel/webflow MCP servers as enabled, causing authentication errors on Cursor Agent CLI launch. Users must manually disable in each project.
incidents.discoveryContext: Filed during governance plan design session. Audited: tool-lifecycle.md MCP sections, setup-cursor-ide-mcp.sh. Session: 2026-03-13.
incidents.suggestedResolution: Stop deploying vercel/webflow to user-level mcp.json. Add per-project only via aitools --addmcp.

incidents.title: Directory backups cascade — each backup contains older backups
incidents.observation: backup_dir copies the entire directory including individual .bak.* files from previous backups. Each new backup contains all older backups.
incidents.expected: .claude/rules/config-file-safety.md defines retention limits (5 directory backups) but backup_dir does not exclude .bak.* patterns from the copy.
incidents.impact: Backup directories grow geometrically. A directory with 5 backups where each contains the previous creates cascading storage growth.
incidents.discoveryContext: Filed during governance plan design session. Audited: aitools-lib.sh backup_dir function, config-file-safety.md. Session: 2026-03-13.
incidents.suggestedResolution: Exclude *.bak.* patterns from directory backup copies in both bash and PS1 implementations.

incidents.title: README 22 versions behind — missing major features
incidents.observation: README.md last updated at v0.33. Current version is v0.54.1. Missing: logging locations, sessions feature, troubleshooting, env vars (AITOOLS_FORCE/DRY_RUN/RUN_ID), MCP status, config.json format, check scripts, governance framework.
incidents.expected: Document intent design principle: every markdown file must state its purpose and be current. README is the first file new users see.
incidents.impact: New users or contributors cannot understand what aitools does or how to use it without reading source code. The README describes a project 22 versions ago.
incidents.discoveryContext: Filed during governance plan design session. Audited: README.md, RELEASE_NOTES.md version history. Session: 2026-03-13.
incidents.suggestedResolution: Full README rewrite covering current CLI, features, governance framework, and troubleshooting.

incidents.observation: Entry points set AITOOLS_FORCE, AITOOLS_DRY_RUN, AITOOLS_RUN_ID, AITOOLS_SUPPRESS_SUMMARY_DISPLAY env vars used by child scripts. Not documented in README, CLAUDE.md, or any reference file.
incidents.expected: No spec exists for: env var documentation convention. Only discoverable by reading source code.
incidents.impact: Users cannot script around aitools or understand its behavior in CI without reading the entry point source. Env vars are a public interface without documentation.
incidents.discoveryContext: Filed during governance plan design session. Audited: scripts/aitools, scripts/aitools.ps1. Session: 2026-03-13.
incidents.suggestedResolution: Document in /aitools skill and README. Add to CLAUDE.md Build & Run section.

incidents.title: Sessions feature silently fails without userRepoPath
incidents.observation: aitools sessions subcommands produce confusing output or silently fail if userRepoPath is not configured in ~/.aitools/config.json.
incidents.expected: PSO: Fail, don't mask. Missing configuration should surface via log_error with remediation instructions.
incidents.impact: Users who haven't run 'aitools user init' get confusing behavior instead of a clear error telling them what to do.
incidents.discoveryContext: Filed during governance plan design session. Audited: scripts/aitools sessions subcommand handlers. Session: 2026-03-13.
incidents.suggestedResolution: Add explicit check for userRepoPath at the start of sessions subcommands. log_error with 'Run aitools user init to configure session archiving'.

incidents.title: Entry point logging override pattern has unclear design intent
incidents.observation: Entry points redefine log/log_ok/log_error/log_warn after sourcing aitools-lib. If lib adds a new logging function, overrides miss it. No validation that overrides cover all levels.
incidents.expected: No spec exists for: when and how entry points may override library functions. script-standards.md documents the logging helpers but not the override pattern.
incidents.impact: If aitools-lib adds a new log level (e.g., log_detail), entry point overrides silently miss it. Log output from the new level would use the lib default format instead of the entry point's custom format. Inconsistent log output.
incidents.discoveryContext: Filed during governance plan design session. Audited: scripts/aitools, aitools-lib.sh logging functions. Session: 2026-03-13.
incidents.suggestedResolution: Clarify in /logging skill and script-standards whether this is intentional specialization or tech debt. If intentional, document the contract (which functions entry points must override). If tech debt, consider an explicit delegation pattern.

incidents.title: CI does not functionally verify installs -- only syntax/build/drift checks (no installer run on any OS)
incidents.observation: UPDATED 2026-10-03: .github/workflows/check.yml now exists (macOS, Linux, Windows jobs). All three run syntax validation, build-deploy.sh, and deploy drift checks only; none executes a setup script or aitools install. Original 2026-03-13 observation ('No GitHub Actions workflow exists') is superseded.
incidents.expected: No spec exists for: whether CI is required for this project, or whether hooks + skills are the intended replacement for CI in AI-assisted workflows.
incidents.impact: Human commits (outside AI sessions) have no automated guardrails. AI sessions have the PreToolUse git checklist hook (planned, governance plan step 8) but it's not built yet. Check scripts exist but are voluntary.
incidents.discoveryContext: Filed during governance plan design session. Audited: .github/ (empty), check scripts, PSOs. Session: 2026-03-13.
incidents.suggestedResolution: Decide: is CI needed for a single-developer project with AI-assisted sessions? Options: 1) GitHub Actions running check scripts on push, 2) git pre-commit/pre-push hooks (local enforcement), 3) accept current state (hooks + skills replace CI for AI sessions, human commits are rare). Document the decision.

incidents.title: CLI entry point behavior only discoverable by reading source
incidents.observation: Entry point dispatch (noargs vs install vs gitpull vs user init), quiet pull retry logic, network detection, flag passthrough to install scripts — not documented in any reference file or skill.
incidents.expected: Document intent design principle: every file must state its purpose. Entry points are consumed by users but have no user-facing documentation.
incidents.impact: Users cannot understand aitools CLI behavior without reading the bash/PS1 source. Debugging failed runs requires source-level knowledge.
incidents.discoveryContext: Filed during governance plan design session. Audited: scripts/aitools, README.md. Session: 2026-03-13.
incidents.suggestedResolution: Create /aitools skill (user-level) documenting CLI modes, flags, env vars, and dispatch logic. Create /aitools-dev skill (project-level) documenting how to add new subcommands.

incidents.observation: setup-user-mcp deploys skills to ~/.cursor/skills/. Whether Cursor Agent CLI discovers and loads SKILL.md files from that path has never been tested.
incidents.expected: No spec exists for: Cursor skill discovery mechanism. Cursor docs do not confirm ~/.cursor/skills/ as a discovery path.
incidents.impact: Deploying to ~/.cursor/skills/ may be wasted work (files ignored) or may cause unexpected behavior. Decision made 2026-03-14: deploy to Claude Code only via setup-user-skills.sh/.ps1. Cursor deployment deferred until this ambiguity is resolved.
incidents.discoveryContext: Filed during governance plan design session. Confirmed during step 4 prerequisite work. Audited: Cursor docs, agent CLI behavior. Session: 2026-03-13, revisited 2026-03-14.
incidents.suggestedResolution: Test Cursor skill discovery: create a skill in ~/.cursor/skills/, launch agent CLI, check if it's loaded. If yes, add Cursor deployment back to setup-user-skills. If no, close this incident and remove Cursor skill code from setup-user-mcp.

incidents.title: Skill deployment hardcoded for 2 skills, needs dynamic discovery
incidents.observation: setup-user-mcp.sh:L378-379 and setup-user-mcp.ps1:L370-371 hardcode two deploy_skill calls (chrome-devtools, a11y-debugging). Five skills exist in shared/skills/ but only two are deployed. Skill deployment is bundled into setup-user-mcp despite being a separate concern.
incidents.expected: CLAUDE.md 'Skills as enablement' design principle: every managed tool gets a skill. .claude/rules/incident-governance.md surfacing duty and governance plan decision #20 require skill deployment infrastructure before building more skills.
incidents.impact: New skills created in shared/skills/ are invisible to Claude Code until manually hardcoded into setup-user-mcp. 3+ skills (planning, optimize-plan, investigate, intent-writing, intent-audit) exist in source but are not deployed. Blocks the entire skill-based governance architecture.
incidents.discoveryContext: Filed during governance plan design. Confirmed during step 4 prerequisite work (2026-03-14). Audited: setup-user-mcp.sh, shared/skills/, ~/.claude/skills/. Session: 2026-03-13, revisited 2026-03-14.
incidents.suggestedResolution: Create new setup-user-skills.sh/.ps1 script pair. Dynamic iteration over shared/skills/*/ directories. Deploy to ~/.claude/skills/ only (Cursor deferred per incident #12). Remove skill deployment code from setup-user-mcp. Wire into entry points (scripts/aitools, scripts/aitools.ps1, scripts/aitools-install.sh/.ps1) and build-deploy.sh.

incidents.title: No meta-skill for teaching ambiguity detection
incidents.observation: Surfacing duty is defined in incident-governance rule (always loaded). /audit provides deep review. No skill teaches agents HOW to identify ambiguities in documentation — the pattern recognition itself.
incidents.expected: No spec exists for: ambiguity detection methodology as a teachable skill. Surfacing duty says 'look for ambiguities' but doesn't teach how.
incidents.impact: Agents follow the surfacing duty mechanically (check cross-references, check for contradictions) but may miss subtle ambiguities that require reading comprehension and domain knowledge.
incidents.discoveryContext: Filed during governance plan design session. Session: 2026-03-13.
incidents.suggestedResolution: Consider whether /intent-audit partially addresses this (it checks content against stated intent, which catches many ambiguities). If a separate meta-skill is still needed, build as user-level skill teaching documentation analysis patterns.

incidents.discoveryContext: Filed during governance plan design session. Audited: script-standards.md, script-standards-detail.md headings. Session: 2026-03-13.
incidents.suggestedResolution: Add 'Bridge pattern' section heading to script-standards-detail.md above the existing double-init documentation. Or fix the reference in script-standards.md to point to the correct heading.

incidents.title: Skills claimed discoverable but deployment infrastructure missing
incidents.observation: Session created 4 user-level skills in shared/skills/ (planning, optimize-plan, investigate, rca) and stated they would be available after restart. shared/skills/ is the source directory, not the deployment target.
incidents.expected: Governance plan decision #20: 'shared/skills/ is source, not deployment. Skills are invisible to Claude Code until deployed to ~/.claude/skills/.' CLAUDE.md 'Specs vs state': never describe a feature as working if it hasn't fired in production.
incidents.impact: User told skills would be available after restart. They are not. Trust erosion — agent described a feature as working that has never been deployed.
incidents.discoveryContext: Found during governance plan step 3 wrap-up. The agent knew about incident #15 but didn't connect it to the suggestion being made. Session: 2026-03-13.
incidents.suggestedResolution: Resolves when incident #15 is fixed (setup-user-skills with dynamic discovery). No separate action needed.

incidents.title: Reference file placed without evaluating alternatives
incidents.observation: path-targeted-hooks-analysis.md was created in reference/ without evaluating alternative locations or consulting the user. Decision criteria from foundational decision #16 were not applied.
incidents.expected: Governance plan decision #16: apply 6-point evaluation criteria (state, context, leverage, risk, precedent, ambiguity) when suggesting. Source-of-truth protection framework: placement decisions for reference files affect downstream consumers.
incidents.impact: Work product placed without deliberation. Precedent set for skipping placement evaluation. The assumption was treated as obvious when it wasn't — alternatives included section in governance plan, plans/ file, or .scratch/ until hooks are built.
incidents.discoveryContext: Found during governance plan step 3 wrap-up. Initially filed as 'reference file created without review gate' — corrected to 'unexamined assumption about placement.' Session: 2026-03-13.

incidents.title: No process discipline rule governs plan adherence or deviations
incidents.observation: During governance plan step 4 prerequisite work, agent proposed pulling step 7 (/aitools-dev skill) forward to before step 4, framing it as 'the skill is small.' No rule, reference, or principle defines what constitutes a process deviation, when resequencing is acceptable, or how to formally amend a plan before executing out of order.
incidents.expected: No spec exists for: plan adherence, process deviations, plan amendment protocols. Audited: CLAUDE.md design principles (governance, ambiguity, specs-vs-state — none address process), .claude/rules/incident-governance.md (tracks defects, not process), .claude/rules/plan-execution.md (code batch mechanics, not sequencing discipline), /planning skill (plan creation strategy), /optimize-plan skill (plan review, not adherence).
incidents.impact: Plan steps can be resequenced ad-hoc without formal amendment. Deviations are invisible — no record of what was skipped or pulled forward, or why. The governance plan's sequential dependencies exist to prevent prerequisites from being bypassed.
incidents.discoveryContext: Executing governance plan step 4 prerequisites (SubagentStart hook). Agent needed /aitools-dev skill (step 7) for wiring guidance. User identified the pull-forward proposal as a process deviation lacking formal justification. Audited: CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/incident-governance.md, .claude/rules/plan-execution.md, /planning skill, /optimize-plan skill. Session: 2026-03-14.
incidents.frameworks: Process deviation (ISO/quality management — doing something outside established procedure requires documentation and justification), double-loop learning (Argyris — the framework itself needed to grow, not just the plan), change management protocols (amend first, execute second).
incidents.suggestedResolution: Create user-level rule ~/.claude/rules/process-discipline.md covering: plan adherence (steps are sequential contracts), process deviation (definition, documentation, approval), plan amendment protocol (amend first, execute second), prerequisite pull-forward (when a later step is genuinely needed earlier, amend with rationale). Add design principle to CLAUDE.md. Alternative: extend .claude/rules/incident-governance.md with a process section — but process discipline is broader than incident governance and applies across all projects, so a separate user-level rule is preferred.

incidents.title: Tool registry is markdown — needs migration to three-layer pattern
incidents.observation: reference/tool-registry.md is a large markdown file serving as both structured data and prose documentation. reference/tool-versions.json tracks versions separately. Two sources that can drift.
incidents.expected: CLAUDE.md 'Three-layer registries' design principle: every registry follows rule + JSON + skill pattern. Markdown registry files are not sources of truth — they drift from structured data.
incidents.impact: Tool data is not machine-readable for /audit validation. Version data drifts between tool-registry.md and tool-versions.json. No /tools read skill for agents to access tool data in context. No per-tool reference files for detailed tool documentation.
incidents.discoveryContext: Identified while establishing the three-layer registry convention during framework adoption work. Audited: tool-registry.md, tool-versions.json, framework-adoption.md registry convention. Session: 2026-03-14.
incidents.suggestedResolution: Migrate to: tool-registry.json (structured data, single source of truth), per-tool reference files (reference/tool-*.md), /tools read skill, /tool-eval write skill. Existing tool-lifecycle.md rule stays. Large effort — plan as a roadmap item.

incidents.title: Incident registry has no read/context skill
incidents.observation: /incident skill files entries (write). /audit skill checks health. No skill presents the incident registry with context for agents working with incidents (read).
incidents.expected: CLAUDE.md 'Three-layer registries' design principle: every registry has a read skill that presents the data with context.
incidents.impact: Agents must read incidents.json directly and interpret the schema themselves. No skill provides context (related incidents, framework references, discovery cycle guidance) when reviewing existing incidents.
incidents.discoveryContext: Identified while establishing the three-layer registry convention. Audited: incident skill (write-only), audit skill (health-only), framework-adoption.md registry convention. Session: 2026-03-14.
incidents.suggestedResolution: Create /incidents read skill (project-level). Reads incidents.json, presents incidents with context (severity distribution, stale items, linked plans, framework references). Distinct from /incident (filing) and /audit (health checking).

incidents.title: Credential storage undocumented; keychain prompts block install
incidents.observation: gh and pup auth checks use macOS Keychain (via their default credential stores), causing 85s delay and 6-8 interactive keychain prompts during `aitools install`. Vercel and Modal were already fixed in v0.36.2 with file-based auth checks. No documentation exists for credential storage behavior across managed tools.
incidents.expected: No spec exists for: credential storage strategy across managed tools. Each tool's auth check was implemented ad-hoc. PSO: Fail, don't mask — but keychain prompts are a UX degradation, not a suppressed error.
incidents.impact: Every `aitools install` on macOS triggers multiple keychain permission dialogs for gh and pup, blocking unattended installs. Users must click through 6-8 prompts. Credential storage strategy is inconsistent across tools (some file-based, some keychain-based).
incidents.discoveryContext: Found during `aitools install` audit on macOS. Timed full install at 6m22s — 85s attributable to keychain prompts. Audited: setup-gh-cli.sh auth check, setup-datadog.sh pup auth status, setup-vercelcli.sh (file-based — already fixed), setup-modal.sh (file-based — already fixed). Session: 2026-03-14.
incidents.frameworks: git-credential (pluggable backends — file vs keychain vs broker), OWASP Secrets Management (platform-native storage + fallback hierarchy), Auth0 Organizations (centralized credential broker for multi-provider auth).
incidents.suggestedResolution: Immediate: file-based auth checks for gh and pup (check token files/config instead of invoking auth commands that hit keychain). Follow project precedent from Vercel/Modal fixes. Long-term: Auth0 credential broker (Nobul Auth0 platform roadmap item) — centralized token management via `aitools auth`, export env vars (GH_TOKEN, VERCEL_TOKEN, DD_ACCESS_TOKEN) so CLI tools skip keychain entirely.

incidents.title: Rules lack trigger directives governing skill invocation
incidents.observation: Of 18 rules, only incident-governance.md has proper trigger directives ('File it via the /incident skill'). glossary.md and frameworks.md were fixed in this session. 6 other rules govern domains with planned skills but have only passive pointers or no skill reference. Agents bypass skill processes when rules don't enforce invocation.
incidents.expected: reference/framework-three-layer-governance.md defines rules as the prevention layer. reference/framework-governed-data-access.md requires every rule governing a domain with a skill to include a 'When to invoke' trigger directive.
incidents.impact: Agent bypassed /glossary skill process despite direct terminology question from user. The glossary rule was in context but contained no enforcement. Root cause confirmed via RCA: agent treats skills as data sources, not process authorities, when rules lack trigger directives. Session 2026-03-14.
incidents.discoveryContext: Found during RCA of glossary skill bypass. User asked 'do we have all these in our glossary?' — agent answered from cached data without invoking /glossary. 5 Whys traced to missing trigger directive in glossary rule. Audited: all 18 rules in .claude/rules/, incident-governance.md (only rule with triggers), glossary.md (passive pointer), frameworks.md (passive pointer). Session: 2026-03-14.
incidents.frameworks: Governed data access (capability-based security, ISO 9001 document control) — trigger directives are the prevention-layer enforcement for the skill-as-capability pattern.
incidents.suggestedResolution: Add 'When to invoke' trigger directive to each rule as its corresponding skill is built. Trigger directive and skill are created together — never one without the other. glossary.md and frameworks.md fixed in this session. Remaining: script-standards.md, tool-lifecycle.md, sources-of-truth.md, interactive-menus.md, agentic-standards.md, cross-platform.md — each addressed when their planned skills ship.

incidents.title: Deploy hooks template embeds 2 of 6 hook scripts; settings.json references 4 missing paths
incidents.observation: deploy/setup-user-hooks.sh embeds only session-archive.sh and standing-order-guard.sh via heredoc. The settings.json merge block registers all 6 hooks (session-archive, harvest-session, scratch-init, standing-order-guard, glossary-skill-guard, sh-file-fixup) pointing to ~/.claude/hooks/ paths. On MDM-deployed machines, 4 hook scripts are never written to disk, so settings.json references non-existent files. build-deploy.sh lines 1457-1796 (bash deploy version) and corresponding PS1 section.
incidents.expected: Pre-commit step 13 (deploy template logic sync) requires deploy/ templates to reflect scripts/ changes. The deploy version should embed all hook scripts that the settings.json merge registers, or the settings.json merge should only register hooks that are actually embedded.
incidents.impact: MDM-deployed machines (no repo checkout) have broken hook configuration. Claude Code silently fails when invoking hooks whose scripts don't exist on disk. Affected hooks: glossary-skill-guard (PreToolUse), scratch-init (SessionStart), harvest-session (SessionEnd), sh-file-fixup (PostToolUse). Only session-archive and standing-order-guard work on MDM machines.
incidents.discoveryContext: Found while adding sh-file-fixup.sh hook to build-deploy.sh during incident #15 extraction work. Noticed build-deploy only reads HOOK_SESSION_ARCHIVE and HOOK_STANDING_ORDER_GUARD but mergeHookEntry registers 6 hooks. Audited: scripts/build-deploy.sh lines 59-70 (hook file reads), lines 1113-1161 (bash deploy template), lines 1171-1241 (PS1 deploy template), scripts/setup-user-hooks.sh (6 hooks in deploy loop). Session: 2026-03-15.
incidents.suggestedResolution: Extend the deploy hooks template in build-deploy.sh to dynamically discover and embed all hook scripts from shared/hooks/. Pattern: same approach used for skills in the new setup-user-skills deploy template (iterate shared/hooks/*.sh, embed via heredoc/here-string, generate deploy calls). The settings.json merge already handles all 6 hooks — only the file embedding is missing. Alternative: strip unembedded hooks from the settings.json merge in the deploy version (simpler but reduces MDM functionality).

incidents.title: Deny rule bypass — permissions.deny doesn't block built-in subagent types
incidents.observation: Agent(claude-code-guide) added to permissions.deny in ~/.claude/settings.json. Built-in Claude Code Guide subagent continued to be invoked, returning inaccurate hook schema (Haiku model) that caused user to disable all hooks. permissions.deny syntax documented as Tool(pattern) but no CC documentation confirms built-in subagent types are matchable.
incidents.expected: No spec exists for: whether permissions.deny matches built-in Claude Code subagent types. CC docs show Tool and MCP patterns but no Agent pattern examples.
incidents.impact: Built-in guide subagent returned wrong hook schema, leading to all hooks being disabled. Deny rule provided false sense of security — appeared configured but was non-functional.
incidents.discoveryContext: Found while investigating why hooks were disabled after adding deny rule. Audited: ~/.claude/settings.json permissions.deny, CC docs permissions page, block-claude-code-guide.sh hook behavior. Session: 2026-03-15.
incidents.suggestedResolution: PreToolUse hook (block-claude-code-guide.sh) created and deployed. Inspects Agent tool_input.subagent_type, returns permissionDecision: deny for claude-code-guide, injects corrective harness context for other Agent calls.
incidents.rootCause: permissions.deny enforces at the permission-request level for user-visible tools. Built-in subagent types like claude-code-guide bypass the permission system (platform-internal, not user-invoked).
incidents.correctiveAction: Created block-claude-code-guide.sh PreToolUse hook. Deployed live to ~/.claude/hooks/.

incidents.observation: settings.json registers glossary-skill-guard.sh as PreToolUse hook at ~/.claude/hooks/glossary-skill-guard.sh. Script file does not exist on disk. Claude Code silently ignores hooks pointing to non-existent files.

incidents.impact: Governed data access detection layer is non-functional for the glossary — agents read glossary.json directly without /glossary skill process.
incidents.discoveryContext: Found during investigation of glossary skill bypass. Agent answered terminology question from cached data without invoking /glossary skill. Investigation traced to missing hook script. Audited: ~/.claude/hooks/ directory, settings.json hooks config, build-deploy.sh hook embedding. Session: 2026-03-15.

incidents.correctiveAction: Tracked by incident #25. No separate fix needed.

incidents.title: Batch size (20+ files) caused cross-cutting rules skipped despite being in context
incidents.observation: Session archive feature planned as 20+ file batch across 5 groups. Cross-cutting concerns (dispatch patterns, encoding, platform guards) got skipped even when rules were in context.

UCI 'Verify subagent audit results' — applies reflexively to the agent's own assertions. The agent had access to scratch-init.sh and the Agent tool description — both were checkable before asserting.
incidents.impact: First assumption: would have produced incorrect audit findings about 'orphaned' scratch dirs and misattributed cleanup responsibility to the wrong script. Second assumption: subagent launched without access to its governing /investigate skill, producing a degraded investigation. User intervened twice to correct — time cost and trust erosion. Pattern recurrence (see #34, #35) suggests the verification-first principle is not yet internalized.
incidents.discoveryContext: Current audit session (auditing b8a9ed4e output). User caught both assumptions in consecutive exchanges. Agent was reading scratch directory contents and harvest manifest when it made the cleanup assumption, then immediately made the subagent capability assumption when launching the investigation. Session: 2026-03-16.

Per the investigate framework escalation rule, 3+ occurrences of the same root cause category requires a structural fix — behavioral coaching (UCIs) has not held. The /incident skill itself may need updating to reflect current harness state and escalation thresholds.
incidents.rootCause: Agent treats internal model of harness behavior as reliable when it is not. Instead of checking the source artifact (scratch-init.sh for cleanup behavior, Agent tool description for capability), the agent asserts from cached/assumed knowledge. Same root cause as #34 (plan drafted from assumptions) and #35 (revision from memory instead of re-read).

The subagent's investigation report (.scratch/session-RTzBnBupE6/channel-placement-investigation.md) contains the incorrect finding. The actual issue (ambiguous placement, not fabricated quote) was identified by the main agent's verification.
incidents.discoveryContext: Current session investigating channel placement at user's request. Subagent launched with /investigate skill to audit session b8a9ed4e. Main agent spot-checked per UCI 'Verify subagent audit results' — searched for the alleged fabricated quote and found it immediately at line 2583. Session: 2026-03-16.

The /delegate skill template for transcript analysis should inject this context. Additionally, investigate whether a transcript-reading utility skill or helper would prevent this class of error.
incidents.rootCause: Incomplete search scope in JSONL transcript. The subagent assumed user messages only appear as type:'human'. Claude Code's queue-operation entries contain the actual user text when multi-line input is buffered. This is a format knowledge gap — the subagent didn't know the JSONL schema.

incidents.title: sources-of-truth.md protected files table exposes all governed registry JSON paths as bypass vectors
incidents.observation: sources-of-truth.md lines 9-33 list all 5 governed registries by full JSON path (tool-registry.json, incidents.json, framework-registry.json, glossary.json, tool-ops.json). incident-governance.md references incidents.json 3 times (L162, L180, L205). documentation-standards.md references incidents.json (L74). tool-ops.md references tool-ops.json (L30). Total: 11 governed registry paths exposed in rules loaded into every agent's context at session start. Scan of all in-context files plus @-referenced files found 26 governed registry bypass vectors across the codebase (excluding plans/ which are working documents, not governance artifacts loaded into agent context).
incidents.expected: governed-data-access.md states: 'A JSON path in a non-skill file is a bypass vector — agents read it and access the file directly, defeating the skill gate.' Rules MUST NOT reference JSON file paths — they should reference the governing skill instead.
incidents.impact: Every agent in every session learns the exact paths of all governed registries from the rules in its context. Proven live: agent read framework-registry.json path from frameworks.md and accessed the file directly, bypassing /frameworks skill. The glossary-skill-guard hook only covers glossary.json — the other 4 registries have no detection layer. sources-of-truth.md is the largest single source of bypass vectors (6 paths) but also the hardest to fix because its protected files table needs to identify the files it protects.
incidents.discoveryContext: Found during comprehensive harness audit session 2026-03-17. Agent was asked to test and verify all managed configs using /tool-ops. User asked 'how do you know about framework-registry.json?' — triggering /investigate RCA that traced the path to frameworks.md (now fixed) and sources-of-truth.md (this incident). Audited: governed-data-access.md, frameworks.md, sources-of-truth.md, incident-governance.md, tool-ops.md, documentation-standards.md. Full scan script produced 26 governed registry references across 47 files (plans/ excluded — working documents, not governance artifacts). Session: 2026-03-17.
incidents.frameworks: Capability-based security (Dennis & Van Horn) — the governed-data-access framework adapts this concept. The file path IS the capability token; exposing it in rules grants the capability to every agent. The skill gate is the access control mechanism being bypassed.
incidents.suggestedResolution: Needs further investigation and barrier analysis (not yet performed). sources-of-truth.md needs a significant overhaul — it predates the framework adoption lifecycle and the governed-data-access pattern. Initial options identified but not evaluated: (1) Replace JSON paths with skill references in the table — but the table needs to identify WHICH files are protected, creating a tension with governed-data-access. (2) Restructure the table to reference governance categories instead of file paths (e.g., 'Framework registry — governed by /frameworks skill' instead of 'reference/framework-registry.json'). (3) Move the protected files table out of the always-in-context rule into a reference file accessed via a skill. For the other affected rules (incident-governance, documentation-standards, tool-ops): replace JSON path references with skill references, similar to the fix applied to frameworks.md and tool-lifecycle.md in this session. Barrier analysis should evaluate each option against the core tension: sources-of-truth.md must name what it protects, but naming governed files by path creates bypass vectors.
incidents.rootCause: sources-of-truth.md was written before the governed-data-access framework was adopted. When governed-data-access was added, the existing references in sources-of-truth.md were not audited for compliance. The step 16 pre-commit check catches @-prefixed references but the sources-of-truth.md table uses plain paths without @, and the check was rationalized as 'known failure' for governance descriptions.
incidents.correctiveAction: Partial: frameworks.md (2 paths) and tool-lifecycle.md (1 path) fixed this session — step 16 now passes. Remaining: sources-of-truth.md (6), incident-governance.md (3), documentation-standards.md (1), tool-ops.md (1) = 11 paths still in rules.
incidents.preventionLayer: Detection — extend governed-data hook (rules-json-guard.sh) to fire on Write/Edit to .claude/rules/*.md when governed JSON paths are introduced. Prevention — update step 16 scope to include plain paths (not just @-prefixed).

incidents.title: Harness launches subagents with a reduced toolset (missing Grep), but standing-order-guard blocks bash grep — leaving no way to search file contents
incidents.observation: A Verifier subagent (session 46ee1c2b) was launched without the Grep tool. Calling Grep returned 'No such tool available: Grep — search file contents with grep via the Bash tool instead.' Calling bash grep was then blocked by standing-order-guard.sh (lines 212-219: first-token grep|rg|egrep|fgrep outside a pipeline -> exit 2 'Use the Grep tool instead'). The two mechanisms point at each other: the platform says use bash grep, the hook says use the Grep tool. The subagent's only remaining way to search file contents was Read with offset/limit. A separate perl content search was also denied. The subagent completed its task only by reading line ranges manually.
incidents.expected: Delegation should never reduce a subagent's capability below the main agent's. The harness's own delegation discipline (delegation-duty-guard.sh, the SubagentStart context-injection layer) assumes subagents are full sensors. standing-order-guard.sh's 'use the Grep tool' feedback (line 216) presumes the Grep tool exists in every session, which is false for at least some subagent launches.
incidents.impact: Every subagent launched without the dedicated file-op tools is blind to content search: it cannot grep, and the guard blocks the bash fallback. This degrades audits, investigations, and verifications (same failure class as #49's incomplete-search finding) — a subagent silently produces less-complete results. Observed live; the Verifier only succeeded via manual Read paging, which does not scale to large files.
incidents.discoveryContext: Surfaced while a Verifier subagent verified handoff-46ee1c2b-1.md. Hit the Grep-absent / hook-block contradiction live, then again on a denied perl search. User directed framing this as a delegation duty / pre-flight concern: 'when we launch agents in our harness we never want to dumb down their permissions.' Audited: shared/hooks/standing-order-guard.sh (lines 212-219), shared/hooks/hooks-manifest.json (delegation-duty-guard, block-claude-code-guide on Agent matcher), .claude/skills/incident/SKILL.md. Related to #48 and #49 (subagent provisioning gaps). Session: 2026-06-20.
incidents.frameworks: Principle of least privilege, inverted — the failure is UNDER-provisioning a delegate below the delegator. Delegation should grant the capabilities the task requires; the harness's pre-flight (SubagentStart / delegation-duty-guard) is the natural enforcement point for a capability floor.
incidents.suggestedResolution: Treat this as a delegation duty / pre-flight check: the harness must launch subagents with a toolset no narrower than the delegator's — never 'dumb down' permissions when delegating. Options: (1) Make the Agent-launch path (delegation-duty-guard.sh / the launch convention) assert a capability floor that includes the dedicated file-op tools (Read/Edit/Write/Grep/Glob). (2) Add a SubagentStart pre-flight that detects a missing dedicated tool and either restores it or warns. (3) As a secondary safety net, soften standing-order-guard.sh's grep/find/sed feedback so that when the dedicated tool is unavailable the bash fallback is allowed rather than dead-ended (hooks cannot easily introspect the toolset, so this is a fallback, not the primary fix). Primary fix is provisioning, per user direction.

incidents.title: Linux is not a defined platform in the governance framework, yet the tool registry declares every tool 'Linux: supported'
incidents.observation: reference/tool-evaluation-criteria.md 'Tool Platform States' defines states 'per platform (macOS, Windows)' and 'Cross-Platform Requirements' names macOS and Windows as the first-class platforms. reference/tool-registry.md marks every tool 'Linux: supported' (= 'Fully integrated -- setup script + installer entry') while every Linux 'Last verified version' is 'pending'. On Ubuntu, typst/uv/go/datadog setup scripts call brew unconditionally. Smoke-test pattern, pre-commit platform note ('(tested: macOS)' / '(tested: Windows)'), managed-file platform table, and the shell-integration brew block are macOS/Windows-only. The CI linux job never runs a setup script.
incidents.expected: No spec exists for: whether Linux is a supported platform, what 'supported' requires per OS (implementation + verification), or how support claims are verified. .claude/rules/cross-platform.md says `.sh` targets macOS/Linux, implying support without defining it.
incidents.impact: Linux users (cloud sandboxes such as Claude Code web, CI runners, Linux workstations) get a registry promising support that silently fails: missing tools, a deleted Go toolchain, a corrupted config. Declared support with no verification also hides regressions on every OS.
incidents.discoveryContext: Same session as #52, during /investigate barrier analysis of why nothing caught the Linux failures. Audited all 26 .claude/rules and 39 reference/ files on main @4c027cc, .github/workflows/check.yml, registries tool-registry entries via reference/tool-registry.md. Session 3030c86a, 2026-10-03.
incidents.discipline: Release engineering -- platform support policy / support tiers
incidents.frameworks: Rust target tier policy: Tier 1 'guaranteed to work' requires automated tests on every merge; Tier 2 'guaranteed to build'; Tier 3 best-effort -- support level is defined by what CI verifies. CPython PEP 11: a platform is supported only with a stable buildbot and a core developer responsible. Both tie a support claim to continuous verification, which maps onto the registry's per-OS status (supported only when CI-verified).
incidents.suggestedResolution: Option A (recommended): add Linux as a third platform in tool-evaluation-criteria (per-OS states incl. distro families apt/dnf); define 'supported' as CI-verified; set registry Linux status to 'evaluating' until the linux-install CI job verifies each tool; add Linux recipes to smoke-test pattern, pre-commit/post-push checklists, managed-file platform table, shell-integration (Linuxbrew path); update shared + dotprofile claude 'first-class' line. Option B: declare Linux unsupported/'n/a' and gate setup scripts with a Linux OS guard. Either way apply the vocabulary decided 2026-10-03: 'platform' = operating system, Claude Code = agent harness, Claude Code web = environment (glossary change via /glossary). Tracked by plans/linux-support.md (to be drafted).
incidents.rootCause: Support declared without a verification requirement; no prevention rule, detection hook, or audit check compares the declaration with reality.

incidents.title: Tool registry prescribes deleting go.dev tarball installs on Linux; 'Install cleanup' rule has no install-before-cleanup ordering

incidents.discoveryContext: Same session as #52. Audited: scripts/setup-go.sh, detect_go_provenance() in scripts/aitools-lib.sh, scripts/setup-typst.sh, reference/tool-registry.md Go section, .claude/rules/tool-lifecycle.md, .claude/rules/tool-evaluation.md. Session 3030c86a, 2026-10-03.

incidents.correctiveAction: v0.73.2 (#33): setup-go.sh/aitools-lib.sh classify the Linux /usr/local/go as upstream and keep it; macOS cleanup runs only after Homebrew Go is verified at the formula prefix; Go registry 'manual tarball' scoped to macOS. incidents.title: Hook rollout rule's enforcement-state table and log path were not updated when standing-order-guard checks were promoted to enforce (2026-03-24) and its log moved to ~/.aitools/logs (2026-06-21)

The deployed hook /root/.claude/hooks/standing-order-guard.sh (identical to shared/hooks/standing-order-guard.sh except a trailing newline) declares no MODE_REST or MODE: lines 46-51 set MODE_AND, MODE_SUBSHELL, MODE_SCRATCH, MODE_OR, MODE_SEMICOLON and MODE_BACKTICK, all "enforce" (OR, SEMICOLON, BACKTICK 'promoted 2026-03-24', commit 154fd46); the glob-in-rm, cat/head/tail, sed/awk and echo/printf-redirect checks pass a literal "enforce" (lines 207-273); `;` is exempt for commands starting with pwsh/powershell/perl (line 178); lines 53-54 set LOG_DIR="$HOME/.aitools/logs", LOG_FILE=standing-order-guard.log (changed from $HOME/.claude/hooks/logs in commit 5a42255, 2026-06-21), written only in observe mode (lines 91-96). Smoke test 2026-10-05 against the deployed hook: `||`, `;`, backtick, `&&`, `$()` and 4-line inputs exit 2; `perl -e "print 1; print 2"` exits 0. `~/.claude/hooks/logs` does not exist; `~/.aitools/logs` has no standing-order-guard.log. Neither commit 154fd46 nor 5a42255 touched the rule. The same stale facts are in .cursor/rules/hook-rollout.mdc lines 11 and 27 and reference/framework-hook-rollout.md line 38; shared/skills/aitool-ops/SKILL.md line 79 lists the hook as 'PreToolUse (Bash git) ... Checklist reminder for git operations' (settings.json matcher is `Bash`). delegation-duty-guard.sh (PreToolUse, matcher Agent, shipped 2026-03-24) is hardcoded observe (header line 6, unconditional exit 0 line 171) and is absent from the rule's table.
incidents.expected: .claude/rules/hook-rollout.md 'Implementation' presents the table as 'Current enforcement state (standing-order-guard.sh)', and the hook's header (standing-order-guard.sh line 28) defers to that rule; reference/framework-hook-rollout.md 'How It's Maintained': 'Enforcement state table in hook-rollout.md tracks current mode per check'; reference/logging.md decision 1: all aitools logging goes to ~/.aitools/logs/; .claude/rules/documentation-standards.md 'Layered reference architecture': one authoritative location per fact. No spec exists for: updating the enforcement-state table in the same change as a hook's MODE_* value or log path.
incidents.impact: Agents load the rule (paths include scripts/**, shared/**, .claude/rules/**) and the Cursor mirror and are told `||`, `;` and backticks are only logged, so they plan Bash calls the hook then blocks (exit 2), costing turns; they are told `;` has unfixed pwsh/perl false positives that were fixed. Anyone following 'Review logs with' reads a directory that does not exist and may conclude the hook never fired. A promotion or reset decision made from the table starts from wrong state; an edit that references `$MODE_REST` as the rule describes, without declaring it, would fail under `set -u` (the I12 crash class in reference/claude-code-effectiveness.md). The /aitool-ops reference card, deployed to every machine, misstates what the hook does.
incidents.discoveryContext: Session 3030c86a-9 (Claude Code web), 2026-10-05. The commander approved 'Proceed with hook-rollout.md update' after an operational-learning note that the deployed guard enforces every check and logs to $HOME/.aitools/logs; delegated mission S5-HookRollout verified it. Audited: shared/hooks/*.sh vs /root/.claude/hooks/ with cmp (17 identical, standing-order-guard.sh and harness-db-sessionstart.sh differ only by a trailing newline), /root/.claude/settings.json hooks block, shared/hooks/hooks-manifest.json, git log -S for MODE_REST, MODE_OR, MODE_SCRATCH and .aitools/logs, .claude/rules/hook-rollout.md, .cursor/rules/hook-rollout.mdc, reference/framework-hook-rollout.md, reference/logging.md, reference/claude-code-effectiveness.md (I11, I12), shared/skills/aitool-ops/SKILL.md, open incidents #25, #51, #59 (none covers this). Per-check smoke test of the deployed hook. Draft updates prepared for review in the same mission.
incidents.frameworks: Configuration status accounting (ISO 10007; IEEE 828): the recorded state of a configuration item is updated as part of the change that alters the item, and configuration audits compare recorded state with the item itself. Docs-as-code single source of truth: derive documented state from the code (or check it against the code) instead of maintaining a hand-written copy.
incidents.suggestedResolution: 1) Apply the drafted updates: hook-rollout.md Phases, Implementation, enforcement-state table (real MODE_* variables, literal-enforce checks, delegation-duty-guard.sh row) and log path; the .mdc mirror; reference/framework-hook-rollout.md artifact path; the /aitool-ops hook row. 2) Detection: a check-pre-commit (or check-post-push) step that parses `MODE_[A-Z]+="(observe|enforce)"` from shared/hooks/*.sh and compares them with the hook-rollout.md table rows, failing on a mismatch or on a variable the rule names but the hook does not declare (e.g. MODE_REST); scripts/check-pre-commit.sh/.ps1 and the rule's Pre-deploy verification list would change. 3) Alternative to 2: drop the hand-written table and name the hook header (standing-order-guard.sh lines 21-27) as the state of record, or generate the table in build-deploy.sh. 4) Prevention: add 'update the enforcement-state table and the .mdc mirror in the same commit as any MODE_* or log-path change' to hook-rollout.md Pre-deploy verification. Open questions for the commander: whether checks with no mode variable and the block-claude-code-guide.sh / block-explore-agent.sh deny hooks are exempt from 'All PreToolUse hooks must go through an observe-then-enforce cycle' (rule line 19); whether delegation-duty-guard.sh, in observe since 2026-03-24, is due for review (mission S4-Delegation owns that hook).
incidents.rootCause: Proposed: enforcement state is recorded by hand in two places (the hook's MODE_* lines and header comment; the rule table and its Cursor mirror) with no check linking them. Commits 154fd46 (promotion) and 5a42255 (log move) changed only shared/hooks/, and no check, hook or rule step flagged the rule as stale.
incidents.correctiveAction: Drafted 2026-10-05 by mission S5-HookRollout, pending commander approval: hook-rollout.md, hook-rollout.mdc, framework-hook-rollout.md, /aitool-ops SKILL.md hook row.
incidents.preventionLayer: Proposed: Detection - check script comparing each hook's MODE_* declarations and LOG_DIR with hook-rollout.md (option 2). Prevention - rule step requiring the table update in the same commit (option 4).

incidents.title: Chrome environment Setup block in tool-ops-google-chrome.md imports only the first proxy CA certificate, fails when the nickname holds a different certificate, and installs without apt-get update
incidents.observation: reference/tool-ops-google-chrome.md 'Environment setup script block' (origin/main) runs `certutil -A -d sql:/root/.pki/nssdb -n ccr-agent-proxy -t C,, -i /root/.ccr/agent-proxy-ca.crt` and `apt-get install -y` with no `apt-get update`. /root/.ccr/agent-proxy-ca.crt holds 2 certificates (`grep -c 'BEGIN CERTIFICATE'` = 2: production interception CA and 'CCR Upstream Proxy CA (staging)'); `certutil -A -i <bundle>` imports only the first (V7-Verify probe). When ccr-agent-proxy already holds another certificate, certutil fails with SEC_ERROR_ADDING_CERT (S6 test case ca-rotated). Root's live store holds ccr-agent-proxy and ccr-agent-proxy-2. S7 test tests/test-setup-block.sh on the base reference: 2/8.
incidents.expected: reference/tool-ops-google-chrome.md 'Requirements': the proxy CA must be trusted by Chrome; the block is described as 'Idempotent'. .claude/rules/script-standards.md 'External command error handling' (apt-get output captured and checked).
incidents.impact: In a new Claude Code web container the Setup block can leave Chrome without trust for the second CA (pages proxied through the staging upstream fail with net_error -202), fail outright after a CA rotation, or fail the Chrome install on stale apt lists; chrome-devtools-mcp then cannot load HTTPS pages and the failure surfaces as the misleading 'running as root' message.
incidents.discoveryContext: Session 3030c86a-9 (Claude Code web), 2026-10-05, delegated mission S7-Detect (finding F2 of mission S6-MCPR4; bundle finding by V7-Verify). Audited: the reference block, /root/.ccr/agent-proxy-ca.crt, `certutil -L -d sql:/root/.pki/nssdb`, S6 test-s6-chrome.sh case ca-rotated, S2 install-chrome.sh (ran apt-get update first).
incidents.frameworks: Idempotent convergent configuration (desired-state): each run compares every managed item with the desired state and converges it, rather than issuing one-shot add commands.
incidents.suggestedResolution: Replace the block with a call to scripts/setup-google-chrome.sh (per-certificate import with stale-nickname replacement, apt-get update retry, logging) plus an inline fallback with the same steps (done on the branch, decision D-ENV9).
incidents.rootCause: The block was written and tested against a single-certificate assumption and a fresh store; the CA file is a bundle and the store is pre-populated in this environment.
incidents.correctiveAction: Fixed on aitools branch claude/fable-status-q9ch93 (S7-Detect PR): setup-google-chrome.sh and a new Setup block whose fallback follows the same rules: each bundle certificate matched by SHA-256 fingerprint under any nickname, imported only when missing, a nickname deleted only when an import needs it and it holds a non-bundle certificate (D-ENV9). A first per-nickname version lost the production CA when the store held the certificates under swapped nicknames (V7-Verify); the fingerprint version replaced it before merge. S7 tests: tests/test-chrome.sh 20/20 (swapped, reordered, rotated, trust, foreign-nickname cases), tests/test-setup-block.sh 12/12.

incidents.expected: .claude/rules/documentation-standards.md 'Layered reference architecture': one authoritative location per fact; checklists must name artifacts that exist.
incidents.impact: Agents onboarding a tool (Google Chrome on 2026-10-05) cannot complete the checklist as written and either skip the item silently or invent a deploy list in CLAUDE.md, a protected file kept under 200 lines.
incidents.discoveryContext: Session 3030c86a-9 (Claude Code web), 2026-10-05, delegated mission S7-Detect (finding F4 of mission S6-MCPR4, re-verified by S7 while onboarding Google Chrome). incidents.title: Claude Code chrome-devtools-mcp arguments omit npx -y while Cursor's and the documented values include it
incidents.observation: setup-user-mcp.sh registers `npx chrome-devtools-mcp@latest --isolated` for the local environment (origin/main line 135; branch keeps it). The registry chrome-devtools-mcp installClaudeCode is the same, without -y. setup-cursor-ide-mcp.sh, registry installCursor and reference/managed-file-deployment.md use `npx -y chrome-devtools-mcp@latest --isolated`. In the Claude Code web environment both scripts now use -y (D-CHR2).
incidents.expected: .claude/rules/managed-file-deployment.md 'Platform-specific config values': one documented value per platform for the chrome-devtools command; .claude/rules/deploy-paths.md: equivalent results across paths. No spec says whether the Claude Code and Cursor commands must match.
incidents.impact: Two tools on the same machine launch the same server with different npx behaviour (confirmation prompt handling for a missing package differs with and without -y; not verified for the non-TTY stdio case), and documentation disagrees with what is deployed, so drift checks cannot tell intended from accidental differences.
incidents.discoveryContext: Session 3030c86a-9 (Claude Code web), 2026-10-05, delegated mission S7-Detect (finding F5 of mission S6-MCPR4). Audited: scripts/setup-user-mcp.sh/.ps1, scripts/setup-cursor-ide-mcp.sh/.ps1, registry entry chrome-devtools-mcp (via /tool-registry), reference/managed-file-deployment.md, reference/tool-registry.md. Left unchanged in S7 to keep local behaviour identical.
incidents.suggestedResolution: Decide whether Claude Code's local args gain -y. If yes: setup-user-mcp.sh/.ps1 (args and the match string), registry installClaudeCode, reference/tool-registry.md; note that existing installs will be re-added once. If no: record why in the registry notes and the managed-file-deployment table.

incidents.title: No rule governed environment branches (Claude Code web vs local) as distinct from platform branches
incidents.observation: .claude/rules/cross-platform.md (origin/main) covers platform pairs, OS guards and 'Dead code from platform guards' only. Linux-only environment behaviour (Claude Code web, D-CHR1/D-CHR2) has two conflicting readings: 'every script must have both variants' vs 'do not write branches for the rejected platform below an OS guard'. The libraries had IS_MACOS/IS_WINDOWS and no environment value; S6 prototyped a per-caller detect_aitools_environment helper.
incidents.expected: No spec existed for: how scripts detect the environment, when an environment branch is allowed, how PowerShell parity applies, how hooks detect it, and how a not-applicable step is reported.
incidents.impact: Each script would invent its own detection (reading CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE directly, root or display probes), and summary rows would differ (WARN vs OK vs absent), so sandbox-off args could reach hosts they were not decided for.
incidents.discoveryContext: Session 3030c86a-9 (Claude Code web), 2026-10-05, delegated mission S7-Detect (finding F6 of mission S6-MCPR4; S7 inventory of 101 files). Audited: .claude/rules/cross-platform.md, .cursor/rules/cross-platform.mdc, reference/cross-platform-detail.md, scripts/aitools-lib.sh/.ps1, governed terms platform and environment (/glossary).
incidents.frameworks: Feature detection over identity detection (capability checks); a single source of environment truth resolved once and passed down (twelve-factor config).
incidents.suggestedResolution: D-ENV0..D-ENV9: environment API in both libraries, 'One script per tool' and 'Environment branches' sections in cross-platform.md and the .mdc, detail in cross-platform-detail.md (done on the branch). Remaining: hook block identity check (rollout batch R4).
incidents.rootCause: The harness assumed two local platforms; the Claude Code web environment arrived (2026-10) without a governance update.
incidents.correctiveAction: Fixed on aitools branch claude/fable-status-q9ch93 (S7-Detect PR): API (tests/test-env-api.sh 87/87, tests/test-env-api-ps1.sh 25/25) and rule amendments.
incidents.preventionLayer: Prevention - cross-platform.md 'Environment branches'; Detection - planned hook-block identity check (R4).

incidents.title: Agent-proxy port in the Claude Code web environment changes between proxy restarts, but the Chrome evaluation record states a fixed port and no harness doc says to read HTTPS_PROXY
incidents.observation: S6 (2026-10-05, about 02:45Z) saw /root/.ccr/README.md (rewritten 02:40:48) give proxy port 39653 while $HTTPS_PROXY/__agentproxy/status answered on 44177. At 03:58Z both README (lines 3, 12, 88) and HTTPS_PROXY give 127.0.0.1:39515: the mismatch no longer reproduces, and the port has changed twice in one session. reference/evaluations/google-chrome-linux-2026-10-05.md line 47 records `HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:44177`. README line 8 says the 'browser NSS store ... already set up'; the tool-ops reference says it was not at evaluation time, and root's store now holds ccr-agent-proxy and ccr-agent-proxy-2.
incidents.expected: No spec exists for: which environment-provided values (proxy URL, CA path) harness docs may record literally and which must be read at run time.
incidents.impact: An agent copying the port from the evaluation record or a stale README into a curl or tool config gets connection refused and may misdiagnose the proxy; claims in the environment README cannot be relied on without checking.
incidents.discoveryContext: Session 3030c86a-9 (Claude Code web), 2026-10-05, delegated mission S7-Detect (finding F7 of mission S6-MCPR4; re-checked by S7: README, `printenv HTTPS_PROXY`, grep of both worktrees for 39653/44177/39515).
incidents.suggestedResolution: Annotate the evaluation record's proxy row as an observation ('port varies; read $HTTPS_PROXY'). Add a line to reference/tool-ops-google-chrome.md (or the environment CLAUDE.md) that the proxy URL comes from HTTPS_PROXY. Close if the commander considers the README out of scope (environment-owned).

incidents.title: Post-push MCP config check verifies only chrome-devtools and --isolated, not the environment's required arguments
incidents.observation: scripts/check-post-push.sh step 3 'MCP config integrity' greps ~/.claude.json and ~/.cursor/mcp.json for 'chrome-devtools' and 'isolated' only (lines 80-87); .ps1 lines 96-97 the same. Step 15 'MCP config deploy' is step_skip. Nothing checks --headless/--chromeArg=--no-sandbox in Claude Code web or their absence locally.
incidents.expected: .claude/rules/managed-file-deployment.md 'Platform-specific config values' (now with the Claude Code web row): scripts must not write another platform's or environment's values; reference/tool-ops-google-chrome.md D-CHR2.
incidents.impact: A regression that drops the D-CHR2 args in Claude Code web, or writes sandbox-off args on a local machine, passes post-push checks; the first sign is a broken chrome-devtools session or an unsandboxed local Chrome.
incidents.discoveryContext: Session 3030c86a-9 (Claude Code web), 2026-10-05, delegated mission S7-Detect (finding F8 of mission S6-MCPR4). Audited: scripts/check-post-push.sh steps 3 and 15, scripts/check-post-push.ps1, reference/tool-ops-google-chrome.md.
incidents.suggestedResolution: Rollout batch R3: step 3 sources the environment API and checks the expected arg list per environment (claude-code-web: --headless and --chromeArg=--no-sandbox present; local: absent). The .ps1 checks the local values only (D-ENV4).

incidents.observation: shared/hooks/tool-ops-session-audit.sh lines 22-29 search `$AITOOLS_REPO_PATH/reference/tool-ops.json` and `$HOME/repos/aitools/reference/tool-ops.json` and `exit 0` when neither exists. tool-ops.json is at registries/tool-ops.json (added there in b504c43, 2026-03-28); no reference/*.json exists. Line 32 sets log_dir="$HOME/.claude/hooks/logs" (tool-ops-audit.jsonl). It also ignores repoPath in ~/.aitools/config.json.
incidents.expected: reference/logging.md decision 1: all aitools logging goes to ~/.aitools/logs/; .claude/rules/tool-ops.md and reference/framework-tool-ops.md: the SessionEnd audit runs the registry's verification cases.
incidents.impact: The SessionEnd tool-ops audit has silently done nothing since 2026-03-28 on every machine: no drift detection or KPIs for audit-mode capabilities. Fixing only the path would start writing logs outside the unified log directory.
incidents.discoveryContext: Session 3030c86a-9 (Claude Code web), 2026-10-05, delegated mission S7-Detect (finding F3 of mission S5-HookRollout; registry-path half found by S7 while verifying it). Audited: shared/hooks/tool-ops-session-audit.sh, registries/, git log --diff-filter=A for registries/tool-ops.json, reference/logging.md.
incidents.suggestedResolution: Rollout batch R2: resolve the repo from ~/.aitools/config.json repoPath (fallback ~/repos/aitools), read registries/tool-ops.json, log to ~/.aitools/logs/tool-ops-audit.jsonl, and log one line when the registry is not found instead of a silent exit. Add the hook to the logging-migration list.
incidents.rootCause: The 2026-03-28 registry move and the 2026-06 logging migration updated scripts but not this hook; no check exercises SessionEnd hooks end to end.

incidents.title: Hook telemetry is dropped when the session's working directory is not inside a git repository
incidents.observation: scratch-init.sh line 35-38 falls back to $(pwd) when `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` fails and writes <cwd>/.scratch/.current-session. The PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks build _cs_file="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || echo "")/.scratch/.current-session" (standing-order-guard.sh 64, delegation-duty-guard.sh 56, glossary-skill-guard.sh 11, block-claude-code-guide.sh 19, block-explore-agent.sh 23, sh-file-fixup.sh 21), i.e. /.scratch/.current-session outside a repo. In this environment the session cwd is /home/user (not a repo): /home/user/.scratch/.current-session exists, and this session's events.jsonl has 0 hook_block events although the guard blocked calls.
incidents.expected: .claude/rules/hook-rollout.md 'Implementation': each block is a hook_block event in <session dir>/events.jsonl when the root has .scratch/.current-session; scratch-init.sh and the hooks must resolve the same root.
incidents.impact: In Claude Code web (always cwd /home/user) and any local session started outside a repo, no guard blocks or delegation events are recorded, so hook-rollout reviews and session KPIs undercount to zero.
incidents.discoveryContext: Session 3030c86a-9 (Claude Code web), 2026-10-05, delegated mission S7-Detect (finding F7 of mission S5-HookRollout; re-verified by S7 with grep of shared/hooks and the session's events.jsonl).
incidents.suggestedResolution: Rollout batch R1: change the six hooks' fallback from "" to "$(pwd)" to match scratch-init.sh (verbatim edits in S7-plan). Alternative: a shared resolver block embedded like the environment block.
incidents.rootCause: scratch-init.sh gained a $(pwd) fallback; the hooks copied an older one-line resolver with an empty fallback.

incidents.title: SessionStart handoff discovery globs handoffs/handoff* but harvested handoffs are named YYYY-MM-DD_session-<prefix>_handoff*
incidents.observation: shared/hooks/scratch-init.sh line 77: `for hf in "$HANDOFFS_DIR"/handoff*`. scripts/ait-harvest.py lines 801-804 route scratch files starting with 'handoff' to `{today}_session-{prefix}_{filename}`, which never matches that glob. shared/skills/handoff/SKILL.md line 311 names `<session-date>_<session-prefix>.md`, also unmatched. .aitools/channel/handoffs/ holds 6 files; the glob finds 2 (handoff-2d439e32-3.md, handoff-46ee1c2b-1.md) and misses 2026-06-20/21_session-46ee1c2b-1_handoff-verification.md and the two 2026-03-2x_session-*.md files.
incidents.expected: .claude/rules/aitools-workspace.md: channel/handoffs/ holds handoff prompts from completed sessions (see /handoff skill); scratch-init.sh header: 'Discovers handoffs at .aitools/channel/handoffs/ (R3, #53)'.
incidents.impact: A new session is not told about handoffs that the harvester routed, so carry-forward work from abruptly ended sessions is missed and the latest-handoff hint can point at an older file.
incidents.discoveryContext: Session 3030c86a-9 (Claude Code web), 2026-10-05, delegated mission S7-Detect (S4-Delegation manifest section 8 item 2; re-verified by S7: grep of scratch-init.sh, ait-harvest.py, handoff SKILL.md, listing of .aitools/channel/handoffs/).
incidents.suggestedResolution: Rollout batch R9: one naming convention (e.g. keep the date prefix and glob `*handoff*` plus `*_session-*.md`), applied in scratch-init.sh, ait-harvest.py and the /handoff skill; a test in tests/ that routes a handoff and runs discovery.

incidents.title: Harvest classifier treats any .md whose name contains log, output or dump as ephemeral, discarding delegate files such as S2-Catalog.md
incidents.observation: scripts/ait-harvest.py _is_ephemeral line 717: `if "log" in lower or "output" in lower or "dump" in lower: return True` for .md files. Substring match: 'S2-Catalog.md', 'changelog-notes.md', 'S3-dialogue.md' are classified ephemeral and not harvested. shared/skills/delegate/SKILL.md line 55 tells delegates to avoid log, output and dump in names, documenting the workaround. harvest_scratch only iterates top-level files of the session dir (line 787), so files in delegate subdirectories are not harvested at all.
incidents.expected: .claude/rules/artifact-harvesting.md 'What MUST be harvested' (research, analysis outputs) and 'What MUST NOT be harvested' (build/check logs, temp output captures): classification by what a file is, not by substrings of its name.
incidents.impact: Delegate reports and research whose names happen to contain those letters are dropped at SessionEnd; with D-DEL1 prefixes (S<n>-<Name>) every delegate name is a candidate, so loss depends on naming luck.
incidents.discoveryContext: Session 3030c86a-9 (Claude Code web), 2026-10-05, delegated mission S7-Detect (S4-Delegation manifest section 8 item 11; re-verified by S7: read of ait-harvest.py lines 703-811 and the delegate skill).
incidents.suggestedResolution: Rollout batch R9: match whole name tokens after the D-DEL1 prefix (e.g. a regex on `(^|[-_.])(log|output|dump)([-_.]|$)`), add unit cases (S2-Catalog.md harvested, build-log.md not); decide whether subdirectories of the session dir are harvested. Then drop the naming caveat from the delegate skill.
